title: The in-between you asked for: a burn that stops halfway
question: Is the middle one what you meant by an in-between — a fire that eats a patch of the meadow and stops, leaving a mosaic?
context_md:
You said of the last two cards: *"an inbetween everything burns and nothing burns would be good"*. **It already does this — I showed you the two extremes, which was a bad choice of demo for that question.** Sorry; here is the middle.

Same sward all three times, same ignition, one number different: how wet the ground is.

Swept finely on one sward, cells consumed of 1,993:

| ground wetness | consumed | front reached |
|---|---|---|
| 0.00 | **1993 (all)** | x=488 |
| 0.20 | 442 (22%) | x=110 |
| 0.30 | 1599 (80%) | x=386 |
| 0.40 | **440 (22%)** | x=110 |
| 0.50 | 229 (11%) | x=100 |
| 0.60 | 137 (7%) | x=63 |
| 1.00 | 10 (0.5%) | x=53 |

**One thing to be straight about: it is not a dial.** Fire spread is a percolation, so at a given wetness the outcome turns on whether the front happens to cross one particular gap — which is why 0.30 burns 80% and 0.40 burns 22%. Across 12 different swards the same pattern held: at bone dry, 5 of 12 burned out entirely and the other 7 landed between 11% and 42%. So partial burns are the *common* case and total ones are the extreme; what I cannot give you is a knob that reliably says "burn exactly half".

If you want the in-between to be more reliable rather than more common, say so and I will look at what makes the threshold that sharp — but I did not want to retune something you might already be happy with.

Also: these are rendered with the **orange** fire colour you picked on the other card.
